DIAGNOSIS READY: Venous Stasis Ulcer secondary to Chronic Venous Insufficiency.

The clinical picture of a chronic wound on the right lower leg in a 57-year-old male, with a 10-year history of bilateral leg swelling, family history of similar issues, and a prior DVT, is classic for venous insufficiency. The wound has likely been present for 6 months, consistent with a stasis ulcer that fails to heal due to venous hypertension. Venous Doppler ultrasound and phlebography have been requested to confirm the diagnosis.
